Each socket `stop()` closes abandons its turn, so a deploy that stops the server abandons every turn in flight unless connections are drained first.\n\n### 11.3 Reconnection\n\nIf the connection drops unexpectedly, the client SHOULD reconnect using exponential backoff:\n\n- Base delay: 1,000 ms\n- Formula: `min(1000 * 2^retryCount + jitter, 31000)` where jitter is 0-1000 ms random\n- Maximum retries: 5\n- On reconnection success, any queued `user_message` messages MUST be flushed immediately.\n- On reconnection, the client MUST clear its local entries array and SHOULD send `?sessionId=` with the id from its last `connected` frame. When the server has resume enabled and the conversation is the user's own, it answers `resumed: true` and replays the conversation; otherwise the client is starting a new session.\n- An entry still streaming when its conversation is resumed is replayed with `isStreaming: false` and `truncated: true`: the rest of its turn streams to the connection that started it, so this one would wait for a commit that never comes ([validated by: replays an entry whose turn is still running as finished and truncated, leaving the stored entry as it is](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L364)).\n- With the server's `latest` option, a client that has lost the id, after a page refresh for instance, MAY connect without one and still rejoin its user's most recent conversation, and sends `?new=1` to start a new conversation instead ([validated by: with latest on, rejoins the most recently active session of a user whose connect names none](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L428), [validated by: with latest on, starts a new session for a user with none, and on ?new=1 even when one exists](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L445)).\n\nAfter 5 failed attempts, the client MUST stop reconnecting and report a disconnected state.\n\n## 12. Security Considerations\n\n- Access tokens are transmitted in the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` request header, which keeps them out of the request line and so out of a URL-based access log. They are not hidden from logging in general: an ingress or proxy that captures request headers records them, as it records an `Authorization` header, so header capture must redact `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` too.\n- The server answers with the `hal.v1` marker, so the token is never written into the 101 response headers or held as the connected socket's `protocol` property. An offer without the marker is answered with no subprotocol, so no offered value is ever echoed.\n- No offered subprotocol value is written to the engine's own log at any level. Every place a credential exists during a connection - request headers, the socket's and the session's `authHeaders`, and the tool context - is listed in [the subprotocol marker spec](../hal-engine-subprotocol-marker/spec.md#where-a-credential-exists).\n- Message content is validated at the server boundary. Content exceeding 10,000 characters is rejected.\n- The server validates all incoming messages against known types. Unrecognized types receive an `INVALID_MESSAGE` error.\n\n## 13. Source Files\n\n| Concern                  | File                                              |\n| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |\n| Shared entry types       | `src/types/session.ts`                            |\n| Backend message types    | `src/types/messages.ts`                           |\n| Backend sender helpers   | `src/transport/ws/sender.ts`                      |\n| Message validation       | `src/transport/ws/validation.ts`                  |\n| Message handling         | `src/transport/ws/messageHandler.ts`              |\n| Connection handler       | `src/transport/ws/connectionHandler.ts`           |\n","numLines":658,"startLine":1,"totalLines":658}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_9946848f24164b1fb48b865d","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

connected = frame;\n        client.send(typeof outbound === 'string' ? outbound : JSON.stringify(outbound));\n        client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n        return;\n unimplemented: [{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}],\n      failed: [{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}],\n      logged: [\n        {\n          level: 'error',\n          category: 'ws',\n a provider ends a tool round with no stop.\nconst suppressingMidAnswer: ChatOrchestrator = {\n  processMessage: async () => 'before after',\n  async *processMessageStream(): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    yield {type: 'text', text: 'before'};\n    yield {type: 'suppress_output'} as unknown as MessageChunk;\n    yield {type: 'text', text: ' after'};\n    yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n  },\n};\n\nconst servers: Array<ReturnType<typeof createServer>> = [];\nconst clients: WebSocket[] = [];\n\nconst eventually = async (check: () => boolean): Promise<void> => {\n  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 50 && !check(); attempt++) await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10));\n};\n\n// Silenced for the whole file: the server logs every connection and close, and these tests read frames, not logs.\nbeforeAll(() => {\n  setLogger({debug: () => undefined, info: () => undefined, warn: () => undefined, error: () => undefined});\n});\n\nafterAll(() => {\n  setLogger();\n});\n\n// Each server sees its sockets close before it stops, so no close is logged after the logger above is restored.\nafterEach(async () => {\n  for (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();\n  for (const hal of servers.splice(0)) {\n    const {wss} = hal;\n    await eventually(() => wss.clients.size === 0);\n    await hal.stop();\n  }\n});\n\n// The authenticated user is read per upgrade, so one test can reconnect as someone else.\nconst startEngine = async (\n  store: SessionStore,\n  resume?: SessionResumeOptions,\n  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator = answeringOrchestrator\n) => {\n  const auth = {userId: 'u1'};\n  const connects: Array<{sessionId: string; resumed: boolean}> = [];\n  const disconnected: string[] = [];\n  const hal = createServer({\n    app: (() => undefined) as unknown as Express,\n    wsAuth: async () => ({id: auth.userId}),\n    sessionStore: store,\n    orchestrator,\n    resume,\n    onConnect: (session, {resumed}) => void connects.push({sessionId: session.sessionId, resumed}),\n    onDisconnect: sessionId => void disconnected.push(sessionId),\n  });\n  // Resolves once the server itself has seen its first socket close, which the client's own close can precede.\n  const firstServerClose = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    hal.wss.once('connection', socket => socket.once('close', () => resolve()));\n  });\n  await hal.start(0);\n  servers.push(hal);\n  const {port} = hal.server.address() as AddressInfo;\n  return {auth, connects, disconnected, firstServerClose, base: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/hal/ws`};\n};\n\nconst open = (url: string, token = 't'): WebSocket => {\n  const client = new WebSocket(url, [HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL, token]);\n  clients.push(client);\n  return client;\n};\n\n// One question answered and the socket closed, returning the id the connected frame announced.\nconst firstTurn = async (base: string): Promise<string> => {\n  const client = open(base);\n  let sessionId = '';\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') sessionId = frame.sessionId ?? '';\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'}));\n      if (frame.type === 'stream_end') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  client.close();\n  await once(client, 'close');\n  return sessionId;\n};\n\n// A ping sent on connect is a barrier: its pong can only follow every frame the replay wrote.\nconst connectAndSettle = async (url: string, token?: string): Promise<Frame[]> => {\n  const client = open(url, token);\n  const frames: Frame[] = [];\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      frames.push(frame);\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n      if (frame.type === 'pong') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  return frames;\n};\n\nconst upserts = (frames: Frame[]) =>\n  frames.filter(frame => frame.type === 'entry_upsert').map(({index, entry}) => ({index, entry}));\n\nconst shapeOf = (frames: Frame[]) => ({\n  keys: Object.keys(frames[0]).sort(),\n  resumed: frames[0].resumed,\n  resumeFailure: frames[0].resumeFailure,\n  types: frames.map(frame => frame.type),\n});\n\nconst deferredRelease = () => {\n  let release = (): void => undefined;\n  const until = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    release = resolve;\n  });\n  return {until, release: () => release()};\n};\n\n// Each stored conversation holds one user entry, sent at the given time and reading as its own id.\nconst storeWith = (conversations: Array<[sessionId: string, userId: string, sentAt: string]>): InMemorySessionStore => {\n  const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n  for (const [sessionId, userId, sentAt] of conversations) {\n    const {entries} = store.create(sessionId, userId);\n    entries.push({role: 'user', content: sessionId, timestamp: sentAt});\n  }\n  return store;\n};\n\n// A store with only the required members, so an optional one can be added, replaced or left out per test.\nconst delegatingTo = (inner: InMemorySessionStore): SessionStore => ({\n  create: (sessionId, userId, options) => inner.create(sessionId, userId, options),\n  get: sessionId => inner.get(sessionId),\n  delete: sessionId => inner.delete(sessionId),\n  count: () => inner.count(),\n  clear: () => inner.clear(),\n});\n\ndescribe('resuming a InMemorySessionStore());\n    const first = await firstTurn(base);\n\n    const frames = await connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${first}`);\n\n    expect({newId: frames[0].sessionId !== first, shape: shapeOf(frames)}).toEqual({\n      newId: true,\n      shape: {\n        keys: ['examplePrompts', 'message', 'sessionId', 'type'],\n        resumed: undefined,\n        types: ['connected', 'pong'],\n      },\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('with resume on, answers the owner reconnecting with resumed true, entryCount 2 and both stored entries', async () => {\n    const store = new   const neverIssued = await connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${NEVER_ISSUED}`);\n\n    expect({fresh: otherUser[0].sessionId !== first, otherUser: shapeOf(otherUser)}).toEqual({\n      fresh: true,\n      otherUser: shapeOf(neverIssued),\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('answers a never-issued id with resumed false, resumeFailure unknown, and no replay or error', async () => {\n    const {base} = it('never adopts a requested id as a key: one session, under the id the server minted', async () => {\n    const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    const {base} = await startEngine(store,
